newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Property sales seen boosting Great Eagle 1996 net.
newsitem.headline: Property sales seen boosting Great Eagle 1996 net.

text.p: Great Eagle Holdings Ltd is set to post solid net profit growth for 1996 when it releases results on Wednesday, with sales and rental income at Citibank Plaza providing most of the rise, analysts said.
Estimates for the year ended September 30, 1996, ranged from five percent to 34 percent growth.
The investment holding and property development firm had net profit of HK$820.04 million in the year-ago period and reported interim net profit of HK$637.10 million compared with HK$491.30 million.
"1996 was pretty good. The Citibank Plaza increase in rents and sales at Citibank Plaza will give a big boost," said Geoffrey Palmer, associate at CS First Boston.
He expected net profit of HK$1.07 billion in 1996.

Great Eagle should book a profit of about HK$383 million from the sale of office space in Citibank Plaza, and with 60 percent of leases at Citibank Plaza up for reversion last year, the company should register a 17 percent increase in rentals at turnover level, Palmer said.
Great Eagle said in March last year that a 69.5 percent unit had sold several floors in the Citibank Tower in the Central district to the Hong Kong government for HK$820 million.
Raymond Ngai, analyst at UBS Securities, said he expected the sale to generate profit of HK$395 million and forecast net profit growth of 21 percent to HK$993 million.
"The main driver will be the booking of some profit from property sales. Seventy percent of the profit from the sale of Citibank Plaza will be booked in financial year 1996," he said.
"The rest of the earnings will come from rental income and hotel operations. Profit from the hotel operation is expected to grow significantly this year," he added.
Ngai forecast 20 percent operating profit growth in the hotel business due to an increase in occupancy and room rates.
Vincent Luk, analyst at HSBC James Capel, forecast net profit of HK$929 million.
"Of the total, we are looking for 30 percent from exceptionals, about 15 percent from hotels and the rest mainly rental income," said Luk.
But he said rental income in 1996 should be flat compared with 1995.
"They are still enjoying upward rental reversions but at the same time they have been selling assets, therefore the floor space has been reduced," said Vickers Ballas analyst Desmond Cheung.
He predicted a "mediocre" year for Great Eagle with net profit of HK$860 million.

But he said Great Eagle should reap the benefits of the expansion of its hotel business. "They are now gaining more exposure to hotels and we would see this to be positive because the yield in hotels is higher than interest costs," he said.
Palmer forecast profit of HK$290 million from hotel operations in 1996.

Great Eagle announced the acquisition of the freehold interest of the Langham Hilton Hotel in London in May and said in November that it was acquiring the 365-room Sheraton Tower Southgate Hotel in Melbourne, Australia.
"I think the company has positioned itself to be one of main hotel predators," said Philip Chan, analyst at Yamaichi International. He expected net profit of HK$1.1 billion.
Great Eagle shares rose HK$0.30 on Monday to close at HK$33.10.
